title: Choose the visual world for the Event Ticketing web app
question: The roll assigned Two-Pass Riso. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Two-Pass Riso
options.thesis: A booking is printed in two ink passes; it is confirmed when the second pass lands in register.
materials: riso fluoro pink over federal blue
options.viewport: Top bar with search; events list with fixed card furniture; a Your bookings rail where each status shows its ink passes settling into register.
options.risk: Grain and misregistration tip into costume if used outside status and imagery.

raised.raise: Every event card carries the same fixed furniture in the same slots: date, venue, from-price, rating.
One body size does the work across lists; hierarchy comes from weight and ink, not a ladder of sizes.
Cancel booking sits isolated behind deliberate space, outline-only until focused.
Pink is reserved for the one active thing: the current step or the booking in motion.
Every price, time, seat and ticket code is set in tabular mono figures.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: split-flap station and airport departure boards
options.thesis: Events and bookings read as a live departures board; saga state changes flip like flaps.
options.viewport: Dark shell, events listed as departure rows (time, event, venue, status), bookings strip with flipping status cells.
options.risk: Familiar: most runs for a live-status ticketing app land here, and it can read as a costume.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: The attendee journey as signed decision points: find, book, pay, ticket.
options.viewport: A yellow band carries search and the journey steps; event date and seat count set monumental.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins product clarity; loses audience identification, nobody goes out to an airport.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere fatigues on dense lists.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Events as a ranked roster of characters.
options.case: Loses both axes: events are not characters and ranking hides dates.
options.kept: Fixed furniture in fixed slots on every card.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as coloured divider boards with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Tab rail down the fore edge, one leaf per event.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as documentation, not going out.
options.risk: Heavy layering slows a purchase flow.
options.kept: One text size does the work.

options.label: Developer Console
options.viewport: Tiled panels: events, bookings, saga log.
options.case: Loses both axes: a costume of the tool for attendees, even if reviewers are developers.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated by deliberate space.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The journey as a purple course over fixed terrain.
options.viewport: Map with numbered controls for each step.
options.case: Loses both axes: nothing here is terrain.
options.risk: Map metaphor confuses a list task.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active leg only.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white data field.
options.viewport: Barcode field with events as columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing data hides the task.
options.kept: Tabular mono figures for every number.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A ticket marketplace as Eventbrite or Tixr ship it, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Search hero, photo event cards in a grid, sticky checkout summary.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
